## Summary

On ROCm, merged #60834 writes the DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 indexer K cache in two launches: a Triton pooling kernel into a bf16 scratch buffer, then aiter's `k_norm_rope_mxfp4_cache`. This PR writes the same cache with the existing fused compress + RMSNorm + RoPE + MXFP4 Triton kernel in one launch, adding a ROCm branch that reproduces aiter's rounding, scale and `cache_format()` page order.

- The written pages are **byte-identical** to #60834's, so #60834's scorer, accuracy and defaults are unchanged. Still opt-in via `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}'`; gfx950 only, as before.
- Removes the pooling kernel and its bf16 scratch buffer (3 files, +179/−245).
- Not a duplicate of #60834: it only replaces #60834's K writer. Earlier FlyDSL scorer/planner changes are dropped from this PR.
- No new dependency: uses only the aiter ops #60834 already uses (no ROCm/aiter#5518, no signature probing). No new logits or workspace allocations. `fused_indexer_q.py` is untouched, and the ROCm branch in the shared fused kernel is a compile-time flag that defaults off, so the CUDA path is unchanged.

## Results (MI355X, DeepSeek-V4-Pro)

K writer, per indexer layer per step, CUDA-graph median (same inputs, byte-identical output):

| Tokens | Two-stage (#60834) us | Fused us | Saved us | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 (decode) | 5.54 | 4.33 | 1.21 | 1.28x |
| 64 (decode) | 5.92 | 4.59 | 1.33 | 1.29x |
| 256 (decode) | 6.96 | 5.67 | 1.29 | 1.23x |
| 1024 (prefill) | 6.57 | 5.13 | 1.44 | 1.28x |
| 8192 (prefill) | 15.32 | 13.41 | 1.91 | 1.14x |

DeepSeek-V4-Pro has 30 indexer layers, so this saves about 36–57 us per step.

End to end, TP8, 8K in / 1K out, one session per arm, same image and inputs (`83c078d9` with and without this PR):

| | #60834 two-stage | This PR | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| C16 output tok/s | 780.03 | 780.97 | +0.12% |
| C64 output tok/s | 1518.42 | 1516.73 | −0.11% |
| GSM8K (1319, 5-shot) | 1254 (95.07%) | 1254 (95.07%) | 0 |

The K writer is a small share of a step, so end-to-end throughput is neutral within noise; the gain is one fewer launch and buffer per indexer layer, with identical cache bytes.

## Tests

- `tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_dsv4_mxfp4_indexer.py`: 3 passed on gfx950 (pages match aiter fed by torch pooling; warmup compiles the single launched variant).
- Byte comparison against #60834's two-stage writer: 0 differing bytes in 6 cases (multi-request, 1 to 9207 tokens, unmapped slots, inputs scaled 1e-3 and 1e3).
- GPU results above were measured on main `3d23773f` / `83c078d9`. The latest merge of main only resolved an import conflict in `amd/rocm.py`; the change lines and the files the fused kernel depends on are unchanged. Ruff and mypy pass on the merged head.

> I am thinking we should allocate the decode logits buffer based on the actual graph size instead of the worst-case configuration. The current allocation may consume several GB of GPU memory for runtime batches.
 Thanks for the suggestion. I measured it before deciding, and I plan to keep the fixed max(512, rows) floor for now.

 Performance: no measurable end-to-end difference
 - At kernel level, the tuned grid helps only at small decode batches (rows ≤ 8): 7–29% faster, but that is only about 0.3–1.5 us per call. At rows 16/64 the two are equal.
 - Serving A/B on 8× MI355X, TP1/DP8, mxfp4 indexer, 3 runs per arm. The only difference between arms is the CTA count:

 ┌──────┬────┬───────────────────────┬────────────────────────┐
 │ ISL  │ C  │ 512 TPOT ms (3 runs)  │ tuned TPOT ms (3 runs) │
 ├──────┼────┼───────────────────────┼────────────────────────┤
 │ 8K   │ 1  │ 21.0 / 21.0 / 21.1         │ 21.1 / 21.1 / 21.0     │
 ├──────┼────┼───────────────────────┼────────────────────────┤
 │ 8K   │ 64 │ 35.5 / 35.5 / 34.9        │ 34.1 / 34.5 / 36.1     │
 ├──────┼────┼───────────────────────┼────────────────────────┤
 │ 128K │ 1  │ 21.8 / 21.9 / 21.9       │ 21.9 / 21.7 / 21.9     │
 ├──────┼────┼───────────────────────┼────────────────────────┤
 │ 128K │ 64 │ 166.8 / 170.9 / 184.4 │ 183.6 / 180.7 / 171.2  │
 └──────┴────┴───────────────────────┴────────────────────────┘

 All C1–C64 cells overlap within run-to-run noise. The kernel saves about 10–45 us per step, while TPOT is 20–180 ms. Also, at 128K the compressed max_seq_len is 33280, and with about 8 rows per rank the selector already picks
 512.

 Switching to the default selector as-is would crash
 fp4_cta_info_buffer is allocated with max(512, max_decode_tokens) rows. With max_model_len=1M and rows ≥ 4, the selector returns 1280–4096 CTAs, and AITER raises:

 ```
ValueError: cta_info_out must have shape (at least 1280, 4), got (512, 4).
 ```

 I reproduced this on gfx950 with ROCm/aiter#5518 head.

 If we still want the selector
 I have a tested patch that sizes the buffer from the selector's upper bound, calls default_varctx_parallel_unit_num in build(), and adds it to the AITER ABI probe so older AITER builds fall back to FP8. Host tests pass (51). I
 can push it if you'd prefer this path. One remaining limitation either way: vLLM passes a static max_model_len // 4 as max_seq_len, so the selector always uses the bucket for the configured maximum, not the actual context
 lengths.

 Not covered: AgentX (MTP + 1M context) was not re-run for this A/B.

1. FlyDSL performance vs. Triton

Based on your benchmarks, the FlyDSL path does not outperform the existing Triton MXFP4 path, while adding ~1,830 lines of code and a new backend/dependency. I suggest separating the K-production fusion from the FlyDSL scorer and landing the fusion independently if it can directly produce the RocmPagedMxfp4CacheLayout expected by the existing Triton scorer.

2. Dependency on unreleased aiter

The FlyDSL path currently depends on unreleased aiter#5518 and uses fragile runtime detection of private aiter function signatures, so the real path cannot be exercised on current released aiter or AMD CI. Please land and pin the required aiter version first, then replace the private-signature probing with a stable API/version check; until then, I suggest keeping this PR as draft.

3. Decode logits memory is not accounted for

Decode logits are not reserved during profiling, while prefill logits bypass the workspace manager, which can cause runtime OOMs for large-context, high-concurrency workloads (e.g. up to ~512 MiB of decode logits at 1M context). Please account for decode logits in profiling and allocate both prefill/decode logits through `current_workspace_manager()`, consistent with #60834.

This PR has modified many common codes under `common/ops` folder, please make sure this change will not influence NV path.

I wonder if there is a better solution that we can decouple rocm-specific logics from common path and put them under `amd` folder?

detail.body:
## Summary

On ROCm, merged #60834 writes the DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 indexer K cache in two launches: a Triton pooling kernel into a bf16 scratch buffer, then aiter's `k_norm_rope_mxfp4_cache`. This PR writes the same cache with the existing fused compress + RMSNorm + RoPE + MXFP4 Triton kernel in one launch, adding a ROCm branch that reproduces aiter's rounding, scale and `cache_format()` page order.

- The written pages are **byte-identical** to #60834's, so #60834's scorer, accuracy and defaults are unchanged. Still opt-in via `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}'`; gfx950 only, as before.
- Removes the pooling kernel and its bf16 scratch buffer (3 files, +179/−245).
- Not a duplicate of #60834: it only replaces #60834's K writer. Earlier FlyDSL scorer/planner changes are dropped from this PR.
- No new dependency: uses only the aiter ops #60834 already uses (no ROCm/aiter#5518, no signature probing). No new logits or workspace allocations. `fused_indexer_q.py` is untouched, and the ROCm branch in the shared fused kernel is a compile-time flag that defaults off, so the CUDA path is unchanged.

## Results (MI355X, DeepSeek-V4-Pro)

K writer, per indexer layer per step, CUDA-graph median (same inputs, byte-identical output):

| Tokens | Two-stage (#60834) us | Fused us | Saved us | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 (decode) | 5.54 | 4.33 | 1.21 | 1.28x |
| 64 (decode) | 5.92 | 4.59 | 1.33 | 1.29x |
| 256 (decode) | 6.96 | 5.67 | 1.29 | 1.23x |
| 1024 (prefill) | 6.57 | 5.13 | 1.44 | 1.28x |
| 8192 (prefill) | 15.32 | 13.41 | 1.91 | 1.14x |

DeepSeek-V4-Pro has 30 indexer layers, so this saves about 36–57 us per step.

End to end, TP8, 8K in / 1K out, one session per arm, same image and inputs (`83c078d9` with and without this PR):

| | #60834 two-stage | This PR | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| C16 output tok/s | 780.03 | 780.97 | +0.12% |
| C64 output tok/s | 1518.42 | 1516.73 | −0.11% |
| GSM8K (1319, 5-shot) | 1254 (95.07%) | 1254 (95.07%) | 0 |

The K writer is a small share of a step, so end-to-end throughput is neutral within noise; the gain is one fewer launch and buffer per indexer layer, with identical cache bytes.

## Tests

- `tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_dsv4_mxfp4_indexer.py`: 3 passed on gfx950 (pages match aiter fed by torch pooling; warmup compiles the single launched variant).
- Byte comparison against #60834's two-stage writer: 0 differing bytes in 6 cases (multi-request, 1 to 9207 tokens, unmapped slots, inputs scaled 1e-3 and 1e3).
- GPU results above were measured on main `3d23773f` / `83c078d9`. The latest merge of main only resolved an import conflict in `amd/rocm.py`; the change lines and the files the fused kernel depends on are unchanged. Ruff and mypy pass on the merged head.

> I am thinking we should allocate the decode logits buffer based on the actual graph size instead of the worst-case configuration. The current allocation may consume several GB of GPU memory for runtime batches.
 Thanks for the suggestion. I measured it before deciding, and I plan to keep the fixed max(512, rows) floor for now.

 Performance: no measurable end-to-end difference
 - At kernel level, the tuned grid helps only at small decode batches (rows ≤ 8): 7–29% faster, but that is only about 0.3–1.5 us per call. At rows 16/64 the two are equal.
 - Serving A/B on 8× MI355X, TP1/DP8, mxfp4 indexer, 3 runs per arm. The only difference between arms is the CTA count:

 ┌──────┬────┬───────────────────────┬────────────────────────┐
 │ ISL  │ C  │ 512 TPOT ms (3 runs)  │ tuned TPOT ms (3 runs) │
 ├──────┼────┼───────────────────────┼────────────────────────┤
 │ 8K   │ 1  │ 21.0 / 21.0 / 21.1         │ 21.1 / 21.1 / 21.0     │
 ├──────┼────┼───────────────────────┼────────────────────────┤
 │ 8K   │ 64 │ 35.5 / 35.5 / 34.9        │ 34.1 / 34.5 / 36.1     │
 ├──────┼────┼───────────────────────┼────────────────────────┤
 │ 128K │ 1  │ 21.8 / 21.9 / 21.9       │ 21.9 / 21.7 / 21.9     │
 ├──────┼────┼───────────────────────┼────────────────────────┤
 │ 128K │ 64 │ 166.8 / 170.9 / 184.4 │ 183.6 / 180.7 / 171.2  │
 └──────┴────┴───────────────────────┴────────────────────────┘

 All C1–C64 cells overlap within run-to-run noise. The kernel saves about 10–45 us per step, while TPOT is 20–180 ms. Also, at 128K the compressed max_seq_len is 33280, and with about 8 rows per rank the selector already picks
 512.

 Switching to the default selector as-is would crash
 fp4_cta_info_buffer is allocated with max(512, max_decode_tokens) rows. With max_model_len=1M and rows ≥ 4, the selector returns 1280–4096 CTAs, and AITER raises:

 ```
ValueError: cta_info_out must have shape (at least 1280, 4), got (512, 4).
 ```

 I reproduced this on gfx950 with ROCm/aiter#5518 head.

 If we still want the selector
 I have a tested patch that sizes the buffer from the selector's upper bound, calls default_varctx_parallel_unit_num in build(), and adds it to the AITER ABI probe so older AITER builds fall back to FP8. Host tests pass (51). I
 can push it if you'd prefer this path. One remaining limitation either way: vLLM passes a static max_model_len // 4 as max_seq_len, so the selector always uses the bucket for the configured maximum, not the actual context
 lengths.

 Not covered: AgentX (MTP + 1M context) was not re-run for this A/B.

@shen-shanshan Thanks for the review. I took suggestion 1 and reduced this PR to the K-production fusion only. The PR now changes 3 files (+179/−245 against main):

1. **FlyDSL vs. Triton.** Agreed. The FlyDSL scorer, planner, env flag and their docs/tests are removed. The fused K writer now writes the `RocmPagedMxfp4CacheLayout` (from aiter's `cache_format()`) that #60834's Triton scorer reads, with aiter's rounding. The written pages are byte-identical to #60834's two-stage writer (0 differing bytes in 6 cases), so scoring and accuracy are unchanged. It saves 1.2–1.9 us per indexer layer per step (1.14–1.29x), about 36–57 us per step for DeepSeek-V4-Pro; end-to-end throughput is neutral (C16 +0.12%, C64 −0.11%, GSM8K 1254/1319 on both).
2. **Unreleased aiter.** No longer applies: the PR uses only the aiter ops #60834 already uses, with no ROCm/aiter#5518 dependency and no signature probing. ROCm/aiter#5518 has since merged; the FlyDSL scorer can come back as a separate PR once it is in an aiter release used by vLLM, with a benchmark against the Triton path.
3. **Decode/prefill logits memory.** No longer applies: the FlyDSL logits code is removed, and this PR adds no logits or workspace allocations. It also removes #60834's bf16 pooled-K scratch buffer.
4. **`common/ops` and NV path.** `fused_indexer_q.py` is no longer touched. In `fused_compress_quant_cache.py`, the ROCm branch is a compile-time flag that defaults off and is only set by `amd/rocm.py`, so CUDA launches the same kernel variant as before.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

1. FlyDSL performance vs. Triton

Based on your benchmarks, the FlyDSL path does not outperform the existing Triton MXFP4 path, while adding ~1,830 lines of code and a new backend/dependency. I suggest separating the K-production fusion from the FlyDSL scorer and landing the fusion independently if it can directly produce the RocmPagedMxfp4CacheLayout expected by the existing Triton scorer.

2. Dependency on unreleased aiter

The FlyDSL path currently depends on unreleased aiter#5518 and uses fragile runtime detection of private aiter function signatures, so the real path cannot be exercised on current released aiter or AMD CI. Please land and pin the required aiter version first, then replace the private-signature probing with a stable API/version check; until then, I suggest keeping this PR as draft.

3. Decode logits memory is not accounted for

Decode logits are not reserved during profiling, while prefill logits bypass the workspace manager, which can cause runtime OOMs for large-context, high-concurrency workloads (e.g. up to ~512 MiB of decode logits at 1M context). Please account for decode logits in profiling and allocate both prefill/decode logits through `current_workspace_manager()`, consistent with #60834.

Thanks for the work!
